name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.151.0 — Tests expire at close: a spec's tagged tests are deleted at review close unless they cite a ledger escape class, exercise a script the pipeline itself runs, or pin an opt-in SHALL CONTINUE TO criterion dated on or after 20260911. An AC-ID defined by more than one spec counts as done only when every spec defining it is done, so a number collision can never delete an unfinished spec's tests. The review row records tests:{born,kept,retired} and the close commit carries the deletions; /spec:doctor gains check 20 to run the same rule as a dry run across every done spec in a host, applying only after one question naming the count and the files. 7.150.0 — Approval is bookkeeping: exclusion rows materialize on the client's own walk-page request instead of waiting on a session command, the closing screen gains a "No — we need this" answer beside "Correct", --mark approved no longer refuses on open exclusion rows and instead reports what was agreed and what was left not contested, and the roadmap's parking-lot fence widens to cover not-contested rows alongside confirmed ones. 7.149.0 — Reopening an addressed client request now leaves the row in the exact shape a server render would produce: the accept/reopen pair, the why textarea (cleared) and the See-journey link all hide, the withdraw control (rendered hidden on every addressed article) reveals, and the reopen answers in the shared msg slot with the same saved receipt the ask form uses. The row also remembers a second round — an open request whose thread carries a client reopen reads 'We'll look at this again' and shows a 'You said: ...' line with the latest text, rendered identically by the server and by the client-side handler so a reload never erases the client's own words.
